body.translated_text: Oṃ! Salutation to the Omniscient One!

children.text: kṛtsnasya tantrasya gṛhītadhāmnaś cikitsitād viprasṛtasya dūram /
children.translated_text: Of the entire treatise whose essence has been grasped, which has spread far from the field of therapeutics,
which is honored by skilled physicians — a compilation of the <s>Yogaśataka</s> (Hundred Formulas) will be made. || Yś_1 ||
Having examined the signs of the causes and diseases, by a physician skilled in therapeutics,

children.text: nirāmadehasya hi bhaiṣajāni bhavanti yuktāny amṛtopamāni // Yś_2 //
children.translated_text: the medicines for a body free from <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) become as effective as nectar. || Yś_2 ||
With <s>chinnodbhava</s>, <s>ambudhara</s> (Cyperus), <s>dhanvayavāsa</s>, <s>viśva</s> (dry ginger), <s>duḥsparśa</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>megha</s>, <s>kirātatikta</s> (Swertia chirata),

with <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>aṭarūṣaka</s> (Adhatoda vasica), <s>mahauṣadha</s> (ginger), and <s>dhanvayāsa</s> — one should drink the decoction in fevers arising from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>. || Yś_3 ||
A decoction prepared with <s>kṣudrāmṛtā</s>, <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger), and <s>puṣkarāhvaya</s> (Inula racemosa), in fever predominantly of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
is recommended in fever with dyspnea, cough, loss of appetite, and side-pain, even when arising from all three <s>doṣas</s>. || Yś_4 ||
A decoction boiled with <s>āragvadha</s> (Cassia fistula), <s>granthika</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, and <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula),

children.text: sāme saśūle kaphavātayukte jvare hito dīpanapācanaś ca // Yś_5 //
children.translated_text: is beneficial in fever accompanied by <s>āma</s>, pain, and <s>kapha</s>-<s>vāta</s> — it stimulates digestion and promotes cooking [of food]. || Yś_5 ||
One should prepare a decoction of <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes), <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>abda</s>, and <s>tiktā</s>, with <s>śamyāka</s> fruit,
in fever of <s>pitta</s> origin accompanied by delirium, fainting, dizziness, burning, confusion, and thirst. || Yś_6 ||
One should drink a decoction of <s>nidigdhikā</s> (Solanum xanthocarpum), <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger), and <s>kāmṛtā</s> (Tinospora), mixed with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper),
in chronic fever, loss of appetite, cough, pain, dyspnea, weak digestion, facial paralysis, and nasal catarrh. || Yś_7 ||
Of <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s> (Callicarpa), <s>bhūnimba</s> (Andrographis), <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda), and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (Picrorhiza),
one should drink the decoction well mixed with sugar when afflicted with thirst, hemorrhage, <s>pitta</s>-fever, and burning. || Yś_8 ||
Having decocted the three fruits (Triphala), <s>dāruniśā</s> (Berberis), <s>viśālā</s>, and <s>mustā</s>, with a paste of <s>niśā</s> (turmeric),

children.text: pibet kaṣāyaṃ madhusaṃprayuktaṃ sarvaprameheṣu samutthiteṣu // Yś_9 //
children.translated_text: one should drink the decoction mixed with honey in all types of <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders) that have arisen. || Yś_9 ||

children.text: savatsakaḥ sātiviṣaḥ sabilvaḥ sodīcyamustaś ca kṛtaḥ kaṣāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: A decoction made with <s>vatsaka</s> (Holarrhena), <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum heterophyllum), <s>bilva</s> (Aegle marmelos), and <s>udīcyamustā</s>,

children.text: sāme saśūle ca saśoṇite ca cirapravṛtte 'pi hito 'tisāre // Yś_10 //
children.translated_text: is beneficial in dysentery with <s>āma</s>, pain, and blood, even when long-standing. || Yś_10 ||

children.text: śuṇṭhīṃ samustātiviṣāguḍūcīṃ pibej jalena kvathitāṃ samāṃśām /
children.translated_text: One should drink <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>mustā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora) in equal parts, decocted with water,

children.text: mandānalatve satatāmayānām āmānubandhe grahaṇīgade ca // Yś_11 //
children.translated_text: in weak digestive fire, in chronic diseases with <s>āma</s> complication, and in disorders of the <s>grahaṇī</s> (duodenum). || Yś_11 ||
One should drink <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia), and <s>guḍūcī</s> with urine, combined with <s>mahiṣākṣa</s>,
in skin diseases, edema, abdominal enlargement, anemia, obesity, urinary disorders, and upper respiratory <s>kapha</s> diseases. || Yś_12 ||
A decoction of <s>mustā</s>, <s>ākhuparnī</s>, <s>phaladāru</s>, and <s>śigru</s> (Moringa) with a paste of <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (black pepper) and <s>kṛmiśatru</s> (anthelmintics),

children.text: mārgadvayenāpi cirapravṛttān kṛmīn nihanyāt kṛmijāṃś ca rogān // Yś_13 //
children.translated_text: destroys worms that have long persisted through both passages, and the diseases caused by worms. || Yś_13 ||
With <s>elā</s> (cardamom), <s>upakulyā</s>, <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>aśmabheda</s> (Bergenia), <s>kauntī</s>, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (Tribulus), <s>vṛṣa</s>, and <s>korubūka</s>,

children.text: śṛtaṃ pibed aśmajatupradhānaṃ saśarkare sāśmarimūtrakṛcchre // Yś_14 //
children.translated_text: one should drink a decoction predominantly of <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) in <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary calculus) and <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria) with sugar. || Yś_14 ||
Having drunk the powders of <s>elā</s>, <s>aśmabheda</s>, <s>śilājatu</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>, mixed with rice-water,

children.text: yad vā guḍena sahitāny avalehyamānāny āsannamṛtyur api jīvati mūtrakṛcchrī // Yś_15 //
children.translated_text: or licking them combined with jaggery — even one near death from <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria) lives. || Yś_15 ||
Of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>gokṣura</s> (Tribulus), <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> (Cassia), <s>pāṣāṇabhid</s> (Bergenia), and <s>dhanvayavāsaka</s>,

children.text: kvāthaṃ piben mākṣikasaṃprayuktaṃ kṛcchre sadāhe saruje vibandhe // Yś_16 //
children.translated_text: one should drink the decoction mixed with honey in dysuria with burning, pain, and constipation. || Yś_16 ||
One should drink a decoction of <s>vāsā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s> with <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor) oil;

children.text: krameṇa sarvāṅgajam apy aśeṣaṃ jayed asṛgvātabhavaṃ vikāram // Yś_17 //
children.translated_text: one can gradually conquer all disorders arising from blood and <s>vāta</s> throughout the body. || Yś_17 ||
<s>Rasāñjana</s> (extract of Berberis) and the root of <s>taṇḍulaka</s>, taken with honey and rice-water,

children.text: asṛgdaraṃ sarvabhavaṃ nihanti śvāsaṃ ca bhārgī saha nāgareṇa // Yś_18 //
children.translated_text: destroys all forms of excessive menstrual bleeding; and <s>bhārgī</s> (Clerodendrum) with <s>nāgara</s> (ginger) [destroys] dyspnea. || Yś_18 ||
A decoction made from <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), <s>bilva</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron), <s>pāṣāṇabhid</s>, the three pungents, and roots,
mixed with alkali, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), salt, <s>uruhu</s>, and oil — should be drunk for pains in the hip, shoulder, penis, heart, and breast region. || Yś_19 ||
<s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>ugragandha</s>, <s>viḍa</s> (salt), <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (ginger), <s>ajājī</s> (cumin), <s>harītakī</s>, and the root of <s>puṣkara</s> (Inula) and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea),

children.text: bhāgottaraṃ cūrṇitam etad iṣṭaṃ gulmodarājīrṇavisūcikāsu // Yś_20 //
children.translated_text: powdered in increasing proportions — this is recommended for <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), abdominal enlargement, chronic indigestion, and cholera. || Yś_20 ||
Equal powder of <s>rucaka</s> (salt), <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>mahauṣadha</s> (ginger), to be drunk with <s>śuṇṭhī</s>-water in diseases arising from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> —

children.text: hṛtpārśvapṛṣṭhajaṭharārtivisūcikāsu peyaṃ tathā yavarasena ca viḍvibandhe // Yś_21 //
children.translated_text: in pains of the heart, side, back, abdomen, cholera, and also with <s>yava</s>-juice for constipation. || Yś_21 ||
<s>Pūtīkapattra</s>, <s>gajacirbiṭa</s>, <s>cavya</s> (Piper chaba), <s>vahni</s>, the three pungents, and a bed of salt,

children.text: dagdhvā vicūrṇya dadhimastuyutaṃ prayojyaṃ gulmodaraśvayathupāṇḍugudodbhaveṣu // Yś_22 //
children.translated_text: having burned and powdered [them], to be administered with curds and buttermilk — for <s>gulma</s>, abdominal enlargement, edema, anemia, and rectal diseases. || Yś_22 ||

children.text: dviruttarā hiṅgu vacā sakuṣṭhā suvarcikā ceti viḍaṃ ca cūrṇam /
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgu</s> in double proportion, <s>vacā</s> (Acorus calamus) with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>suvarcikā</s>, and <s>viḍa</s> (salt) powder —
to be taken with warm water; it destroys flatulence, cholera, pain, heart disease, <s>gulma</s>, and upward-moving wind. || Yś_23 ||
<s>Śṛṅgī</s>, the three pungents, the three fruits, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> (Solanum), <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>puṣkara</s> (Inula), <s>jaṭā</s> (nard), and the five salts —

children.text: cūrṇaṃ pibed aśiśireṇa jalena hikkāśvāsordhvavātakasanārucipīnaseṣu // Yś_24 //
children.translated_text: the powder should be drunk with warm water in hiccup, dyspnea, upward-moving wind, indigestion, loss of appetite, and nasal catarrh. || Yś_24 ||
Of <s>nādeyī</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s> (Holarrhena), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), the two <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>snuk</s> (Euphorbia), <s>bilva</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s> (Semecarpus),
<s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Butea), <s>pāribhadra</s>, <s>jaṭā</s>, <s>pāmārga</s> (Achyranthes), <s>nīpa</s>, and <s>agni</s>,
<s>vāsā</s>, <s>muṣkaka</s>, and <s>pāṭalā</s> — having burned them with salt and cooked the juice,
with an admixture of <s>hiṅgu</s> and the like — this is suitable for <s>gulma</s>, abdominal enlargement, and splenic disease. || Yś_25 ||
With equal parts of <s>cavya</s>, <s>amlavetasa</s>, the three pungents, <s>tittiḍīka</s>, <s>tālīsa</s>, <s>jīraka</s> (cumin), <s>tugā</s>, and <s>dahana</s>,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ guḍapramṛditaṃ trisugandhiyuktaṃ vaisvaryapīnasakaphāruciṣu praśastam // Yś_26 //
children.translated_text: powder mixed with jaggery, combined with the three aromatics — recommended for hoarseness, nasal catarrh, <s>kapha</s>, and loss of appetite. || Yś_26 ||

children.text: tālīsacavyamaricaṃ sadṛśaṃ dviraṃśaṃ mūlaṃ tugāṃ magadhajāṃ triguṇāṃ ca śuṇṭhīm /
children.translated_text: <s>Tālīsa</s>, <s>cavya</s>, and <s>marica</s> (pepper) in equal parts, double the <s>mūla</s> (root), <s>tugā</s>, triple <s>māgadhī</s> (long pepper), and <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (ginger),

children.text: kṛtvā guḍatriguṇitāṃ guḍikāṃ sugandhāṃ kāsāgnimāndyagudajajvararukṣu dadyāt // Yś_27 //
children.translated_text: made into a fragrant pill with triple jaggery — to be given for cough, weak digestion, rectal disease, fever, and pain. || Yś_27 ||
<s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), <s>marica</s> (black pepper), <s>nāgadala</s>, <s>tvak</s> (cinnamon), and <s>elā</s> (cardamom), powdered, increasing in order from the last upward,
should be eaten with equal sugar for rectal disease, weak digestion, <s>gulma</s>, loss of appetite, dyspnea, and throat and heart diseases. || Yś_28 ||
One should make pills with <s>sindhūttha</s> (rock salt), <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>yavānī</s> (Trachyspermum), the three pungents, and portions of jaggery;

children.text: tair bhakṣitais tṛptim avāpnuvan na bhuñjīta mandāgnir api prabhūtam // Yś_29 //
children.translated_text: by eating those, even one with weak digestion who does not attain satiety should eat abundantly. || Yś_29 ||
Equal parts of iron, sesame, the three pungents, and <s>kola</s> (jujube), with metallic powder of <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite),

children.text: tair modakaḥ kṣaudrayuto 'nutakraḥ pāṇḍvāmaye dūragate 'pi śastaḥ // Yś_30 //
children.translated_text: a modaka pill with those, combined with honey and buttermilk, is recommended for anemia even when far advanced. || Yś_30 ||

children.text: guḍena śuṇṭhīm athavopakulyāṃ pathyātṛtīyām atha dāḍimaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: One should always eat <s>śuṇṭhī</s> with jaggery, or <s>upakulyā</s>, or <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia) as the third, or <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate),

children.text: āmeṣv ajīrṇeṣu gudāmayeṣu varcovibandheṣu ca nityam adyāt // Yś_31 //
children.translated_text: in conditions with <s>āma</s>, indigestion, rectal diseases, and constipation. || Yś_31 ||
Powder of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>nāgara</s> (ginger), and <s>mustā</s> — a pill should be made with jaggery;

children.text: nivārayaty āsyavidhāriteyaṃ śvāsaṃ pravṛddhaṃ prabalaṃ ca kāsam // Yś_32 //
children.translated_text: held in the mouth, it suppresses increased dyspnea and severe cough. || Yś_32 ||

children.text: vaṭaprarohaṃ madhu kuṣṭham utpalaṃ salājacūrṇaṃ guḍikāṃ prakalpayet /
children.translated_text: Aerial roots of <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan), honey, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>utpala</s> (lotus), and powder of parched rice — a pill should be prepared;

children.text: susaṃhitā sā vadanena dhāritā tṛṣṇāṃ pravṛddhām api hanti satvaram // Yś_33 //
children.translated_text: well-composed and held in the mouth, it quickly destroys even severe thirst. || Yś_33 ||
Powder of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), <s>māgadhī</s> (long pepper), and <s>koṣaṇa</s>, mixed with the sour juice of <s>kapittha</s> (wood apple),

children.text: lājaiḥ samāṃśair madhunāvalīḍhaṃ chardiṃ prasaktām asakṛn nihanti // Yś_34 //
children.translated_text: licked with equal parts of parched rice and honey, it destroys persistent vomiting repeatedly. || Yś_34 ||

children.text: dūrvāraso dāḍimapuṣpajo vā ghrāṇapravṛtte 'sṛji nasyam uktam /
children.translated_text: The juice of <s>dūrvā</s> (Cynodon) or that produced from <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) flowers is prescribed as nasal drops when blood flows from the nose;

children.text: stanyena vālaktarasena vāpi viṇ makṣikānāṃ ca nihanti hikkām // Yś_35 //
children.translated_text: breast-milk or the juice of <s>lākṣā</s> (lac), and also the dung of bees, destroys hiccup. || Yś_35 ||

children.text: dhātrīrasaḥ sarjarasaḥ sapākyaḥ sauvīrapiṣṭaś ca tadāsutaś ca /
children.translated_text: The juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka), the resin of <s>sarja</s> (Vateria), with <s>pākya</s>, ground <s>sauvīra</s>, and its extract —

children.text: bhavanti sidhmāni yathā na bhūyas tathaivam udvartanakaṃ karoti // Yś_36 //
children.translated_text: used as an ointment, it acts so that <s>sidhmā</s> (leucoderma) does not recur. || Yś_36 ||
<s>Dūrvā</s>, <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>cakramarda</s> (Cassia tora), and <s>kuṭheraka</s>, ground with sour gruel and buttermilk —

children.text: tribhiḥ pralepair api baddhamūlāṃ dadruṃ ca kaṇḍuṃ ca vināśayanti // Yś_37 //
children.translated_text: applied as a paste three times, they destroy even deep-rooted ringworm and itching. || Yś_37 ||
With <s>gaṇḍīrikā</s>, <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), <s>mārkava</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, tree bark, and salt, mixed with urine,
one should cook oil — it removes circular skin disease, ringworm, foul wounds, pain, and <s>kiṭimā</s> (scab). || Yś_38 ||
With equal parts of <s>sindūra</s> (red lead), <s>guggulu</s> (Commiphora), <s>rasāñjana</s>, <s>siktha</s> (beeswax), and <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), this pungent oil when cooked,

children.text: kacchūṃ sravatpiṭakikām athavāpi śuṣkām abhyañjanena sakṛd uddharati prasahya // Yś_39 //
children.translated_text: by a single application forcibly removes <s>kacchū</s> (itching), weeping pustules, or dry [skin conditions]. || Yś_39 ||
With <s>suvarcikā</s>, <s>nāgara</s> (ginger), <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>lākṣā</s> (lac), <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), and <s>lohitayaṣṭikā</s>,

children.text: tailaṃ jvare ṣaḍguṇatakrasiddham abhyañjanāc chītavidāhanut syāt // Yś_40 //
children.translated_text: oil prepared with six times the buttermilk, applied externally, would relieve cold and burning in fever. || Yś_40 ||

children.text: sarpir guḍūcīvṛṣakaṇṭakārīkvāthena kalkena ca siddham etat /
children.translated_text: Ghee prepared with the decoction and paste of <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora), <s>vṛṣa</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> (Solanum) —
should be drunk in chronic fever, cough, pain, dyspnea, weak digestion, and disorders of the <s>grahaṇī</s> (duodenum). || Yś_41 ||
With the decoction and paste of <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu), <s>paṭola</s> (Trichosanthes) leaves, <s>nimba</s> (neem) bark, <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), and <s>āmalakī</s> (Emblica),

children.text: ghṛtam abhinavam etad āśu siddhaṃ jayati visarpamadāśrakuṣṭhagulmān // Yś_42 //
children.translated_text: this fresh ghee, quickly prepared, conquers <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), intoxication, hemorrhage, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease) and <s>gulma</s>. || Yś_42 ||
By the <s>doṣas</s> (humors) aggravated in the skin, flesh, and blood,
<s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas) is a particular wasting of the entire body;
<s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is of the nature of liquor; it is the disorder produced by drinking liquor. // Yś_43 //

With the paste-water of <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>picumarda</s> (neem), <s>dhāvanī</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), and <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda),

children.text: ghṛtam uttamaṃ vidhivipakvam ādṛtaḥ prapibann idaṃ jayati kuṣṭham āturaḥ // Yś_44 //
children.translated_text: the patient who carefully drinks this excellent ghee, cooked according to proper method, conquers <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease). // Yś_44 //
Pieces of <s>kuṣmāṇḍaka</s> (ash gourd), steamed by the cooking method, dried, and fried in ghee,

should be placed when the sugar is cooked, together with <s>marica</s> (black pepper), <s>magadhā</s> (long pepper), <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>ajājī</s> (cumin), and <s>trigandha</s> (three aromatics);
this <s>leha</s> (electuary) is beneficial for children, the elderly, those afflicted by wind and blood disorders, the emaciated, women, and those with consumption,
and those suffering from thirst, cough, bleeding disorders, <s>pitta</s>, dyspnea, abdominal pain, and vomiting. // Yś_45 //
Having boiled urine, sour gruel, and honey with <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum), <s>piṇḍītaka</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper), <s>viḍa</s> salt, <s>dhūma</s> (smoke-plant), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea),

children.text: vartiṃ karāṅguṣṭhanibhāṃ ghṛtāktāṃ gude rujānāhaharīṃ vidadhyāt // Yś_46 //
children.translated_text: one should prepare a suppository the size of a thumb, smeared with ghee, to be applied in the rectum for relieving pain and distension. // Yś_46 //

children.text: saśarkaraṃ kuṅkumam ājyabhṛṣṭaṃ nasyaṃ vidheyaṃ pavanāsṛgutthe /
children.translated_text: Saffron with sugar, fried in ghee, should be administered as a nasal remedy when caused by <s>vāta</s> (wind) and blood disorders,
in pain of the eyebrows, ears, temples, eyes, and half the head, and in diseases that increase during the day. // Yś_47 //

One should prepare a collyrium stick with the seeds from the fruits of <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia bellirica), and <s>dhātrī</s> (Emblica), in proportions of three, two, and one parts respectively;

children.text: tayāñjayed aśrum atipravṛddham akṣṇor haret kaṣṭam api prakopam // Yś_48 //
children.translated_text: applying it as collyrium, it removes excessive lacrimation and even severe aggravation of the eyes. // Yś_48 //
With <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s> (talc), and <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), ground with clean water,

children.text: bahiṣpralepaṃ nayanasya kuryāt sarvākṣirogopaśamārtham etat // Yś_49 //
children.translated_text: one should make an external application for the eyes; this is for the alleviation of all eye diseases. // Yś_49 //
<s>Lodhra</s> (Symplocos) with <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), fried in ghee, ground with <s>sauvīra</s> (a type of vinegar), and bound in white cloth—

children.text: āścyotanaṃ tan nayanasya kuryāt sadāhakaṇḍūṃ ca rujaṃ nihanyāt // Yś_50 //
children.translated_text: that should be used as eye drops for the eyes; it destroys burning, itching, and pain. // Yś_50 //

children.text: hanty arjunaṃ śarkarayābdhipheno naktāndhatāṃ gośakṛtā ca kṛṣṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Abdhiphena</s> (cuttlefish bone) with sugar destroys <s>arjuna</s> (pterygium), and <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper) with cow dung destroys night blindness;

children.text: rasāñjanaṃ vyoṣayutaṃ ca pillaṃ tāpīsamutthaṃ madhunā ca śukram // Yś_51 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasāñjana</s> (Berberis extract) with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) destroys <s>pilla</s> (corneal film), and that derived from <s>tāpīsa</s> (copper sulfate) with honey destroys <s>śukra</s> (corneal opacity). // Yś_51 //

With equal parts of <s>puṣpa</s> (Datura flower), <s>tārkṣya</s> (talc), sugar, <s>udadhiphena</s> (cuttlefish bone), conch shell, <s>sindhūttha</s> (rock salt), <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), and <s>marica</s> (black pepper),

children.text: piṣṭais tu mākṣikarasena rasakriyeyaṃ hanty armakācatimirārjunavartmarogān // Yś_52 //
children.translated_text: ground with honey, this <s>rasakriyā</s> (collyrium preparation) destroys <s>arman</s> (pterygium), <s>kāca</s> (cataract), <s>timira</s> (dimness of vision), <s>arjuna</s>, and eyelid disorders. // Yś_52 //
<s>Musta</s> (Cyperus), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), <s>rajas</s> (pollen), <s>yavāsa</s> (Alhagi), <s>marica</s> (black pepper), <s>sindhūdbhava</s> (rock salt), <s>kaṭphala</s> (Myrica),
<s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>tutthaka</s> (copper sulfate), <s>śaṅkhaphena</s> (cuttlefish bone), <s>nalada</s> (spikenard), <s>kālānusārī</s> (a fragrant substance), and <s>añjana</s> (collyrium)—

children.text: tulyaṃ cūrṇitam āyase vinihitaṃ kṣaudrānvitaṃ śasyate
children.translated_text: all in equal parts, powdered, placed in an iron vessel, and combined with honey, this is recommended
for itching, <s>arman</s> (pterygium), eye diseases, bloodshot streaks, <s>timira</s> (dimness of vision), and <s>pilla</s> (corneal film). // Yś_53 //
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Rubia), <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), sea foam, <s>tvak</s> (cinnamon bark), <s>sevya</s> (vetiver), <s>gorocanā</s> (ox bile pigment),
<s>māṃsī</s> (spikenard), <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), conch shell, <s>patra</s> (bay leaf), mineral earth, <s>tālīsa</s> (Abies), flower, and <s>añjana</s> (collyrium)—

children.text: sarvair eva samāṃśam añjanam idaṃ śastaṃ sadā cakṣuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: all in equal parts, this collyrium is always recommended for the eyes,
removing itching, excessive moisture, impurities, tears, blood disorders, pain, <s>pilla</s> (corneal film), <s>arman</s> (pterygium), and <s>śukra</s> (corneal opacity). // Yś_54 //
A decoction of <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus), <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum), <s>indradāru</s> (Cedrus deodara), <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (Picrorhiza),

children.text: gomūtrasiddho madhunā ca yuktaḥ peyo galavyādhiṣu sarvajeṣu // Yś_55 //
children.translated_text: prepared with cow's urine and combined with honey, should be drunk for all types of throat diseases. // Yś_55 //

children.text: yavāgrajaṃ tejavatīṃ sapāṭhāṃ rasāñjanaṃ dāruniśāṃ sakṛṣṇām /
children.translated_text: <s>Yavāgraja</s> (barley alkali), <s>tejavatī</s> (Zanthoxylum), <s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), <s>rasāñjana</s> (Berberis extract), <s>dāruniśā</s> (tree turmeric), and <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper)—

children.text: kṣaudreṇa kuryād guṭikāṃ mukhena tāṃ dhārayet sarvagalāmayeṣu // Yś_56 //
children.translated_text: one should prepare a pill with honey and hold it in the mouth for all throat ailments. // Yś_56 //
A decoction of <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora), <s>sumanā</s> (jasmine) shoots, <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes), <s>yavāsa</s> (Alhagi), and <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits),

children.text: kṣaudreṇa yuktaḥ kavalagraho 'yaṃ mukhasya pākaṃ śamayaty udīrṇam // Yś_57 //
children.translated_text: combined with honey, used as a mouth gargle, alleviates aggravated inflammation of the mouth. // Yś_57 //

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ dārvī lodhram abdaṃ samaṅgā pāṭhā tiktā tejanī pītikā ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos), <s>abda</s> (Cyperus), <s>samaṅgā</s> (Rubia), <s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), <s>tiktā</s> (Picrorhiza), <s>tejanī</s>, and <s>pītikā</s>—

children.text: cūrṇaṃ śastaṃ gharṣaṇaṃ tad dvijānāṃ raktasrāvaṃ hanti kaṇḍūrujaṃ ca // Yś_58 //
children.translated_text: this powder is recommended as a tooth-rubbing preparation; it destroys bleeding, itching, and pain. // Yś_58 //
With <s>sauvīra</s> (a type of vinegar), sour gruel, fresh ginger, <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) pulp, their juices, <s>guggulu</s> (resin), and <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt),

children.text: paktvā tu tailaṃ kaṭukaṃ niṣiñcet tat karṇayoḥ karṇarujopaśāntyai // Yś_59 //
children.translated_text: having cooked oil with these pungent ingredients, one should instill it in both ears for the alleviation of ear pain. // Yś_59 //
With <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda), <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>parpaṭa</s>, fruit, <s>cavya</s> (Piper chaba), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), and water-born herbs,
<s>tikta</s> (bitter herbs), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), <s>durālabhā</s> (Fagonia), <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents), <s>trāyantī</s>, and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood),
ghee prepared with these is effective in disorders above the clavicle, and in pain of the nose, eyes, and so forth,
in skin disorders, fevers, abscesses, wound pain, and <s>śukra</s> (corneal opacity) disorders. // Yś_60 //
<s>Dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>parpaṭa</s>, <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>vatsaka</s> (Holarrhena), <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), <s>duḥsparśā</s> (Tragia), <s>yaṣṭī</s> (licorice), and <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda),
<s>trāyantī</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>kaṭukā</s> (Picrorhiza), <s>bhūnimba</s> (Andrographis), and <s>raktāmbu</s> (red aquatic plant)—

children.text: eṣāṃ kalkakaṣāyasādhitam idaṃ sarpiḥ praśastaṃ dṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: ghee prepared with the paste and decoction of these is recommended for the eyes,
in disorders arising from <s>pitta</s> and blood, <s>śukra</s> (corneal opacity), <s>timira</s> (dimness of vision), and diseases of the upper body. // Yś_61 //

children.text: śuklairaṇḍān mūlam athogrā śatapuṣpā puṣpodbhūtaṃ yac ca bṛhatyās tagaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The root of white <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), <s>ugrā</s> (Achyranthes), <s>śatapuṣpā</s> (dill), the flowers of <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), and <s>tagara</s> (valerian)—

children.text: tailaṃ siddhaṃ taiḥ sapayaskais timiraghnaṃ nasyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vyādhiṣu cordhveṣv apareṣu // Yś_62 //
children.translated_text: oil prepared with these along with milk, destroying <s>timira</s> (dimness of vision), is the best nasal remedy for upper body and other diseases. // Yś_62 //
In a decoction of <s>muṣkaka</s> (Schrebera) ash, one should place conch shell burnt in fire;

children.text: tat tenaiva punar jalena vipacet kṣāraṃ sa taile vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: then one should cook the alkali again with that same water—this is the procedure for the oil preparation.

children.text: yuñjyāt tad vraṇaduṣṭiṣu vraṇarujāsv arśassu nāḍīṣu ca
children.translated_text: One should apply it in wound infections, wound pain, <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), and <s>nāḍī</s> (sinus tracts),

children.text: tvagdoṣeṣu bhagaṃdareṣu vividhe kaṇṭhāmaye ca sthire // Yś_63 //
children.translated_text: in skin disorders, <s>bhagaṃdara</s> (fistula-in-ano), and in various chronic throat diseases. // Yś_63 //

With <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), <s>yaṣṭīmadhu</s> (licorice), <s>padmaka</s> (wild cherry), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>priyaṅgu</s> (Callicarpa), <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos), and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood),

children.text: vipācya tailaṃ payasā prayojayet kṣateṣu saṃropaṇadāhanāśanam // Yś_64 //
children.translated_text: having cooked oil with milk, one should apply it to wounds—it promotes healing and destroys burning sensation. // Yś_64 //
<s>Jātī</s> (jasmine), <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) leaves, <s>kaṭukā</s> (Picrorhiza), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), <s>sārivā</s> (Hemidesmus),

<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Rubia), <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>siktha</s> (beeswax), <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), and <s>naktāhva</s> (Holarrhena) seeds, in equal parts—

children.text: sarpiḥ siddham anena sūkṣmavadanā marmāśritāḥ srāvino
children.translated_text: ghee prepared with these heals wounds that have narrow openings, are seated in vital points, and are discharging,

children.text: gambhīrāḥ sarujā vraṇāḥ sagatikāḥ śudhyanti rohanti ca // Yś_65 //
children.translated_text: deep, painful, and with sinuses—they become purified and heal. // Yś_65 //

children.text: śirīṣapuṣpaṃ svarasena bhāvitaṃ sahasrakṛtvo maricaṃ sitāhvayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śirīṣa</s> (Albizia) flower soaked in its own juice a thousand times, and white <s>marica</s> (pepper)—

children.text: prayojayed añjanapānanāvanair vimohitānām api sarpadaṃśinām // Yś_66 //
children.translated_text: one should administer it as collyrium, drink, and nasal drops for those who have lost consciousness from snake bites. // Yś_66 //

children.text: mayūrapittena tu taṇḍulīyakaṃ kākāṇḍayuktaṃ prapibed analpam /
children.translated_text: <s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus) with peacock bile and <s>kākāṇḍa</s> (Abrus seeds) should be drunk in substantial quantity;

children.text: viṣāṇi saṃstāvarajaṅgamāni sopadravāṇy apy acireṇa hanti // Yś_67 //
children.translated_text: it destroys both plant-based and animal-based poisons, even those with complications, in a short time. // Yś_67 //

children.text: tailaṃ tilānāṃ palalaṃ guḍaṃ ca kṣīraṃ tathārkaṃ samam eva pītam /
children.translated_text: Sesame oil, sesame cake, jaggery, milk, and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) juice, drunk in equal parts,

children.text: ālarkam ugraṃ viṣam āśu hanti sadyodbhavaṃ vāyur ivābhravṛndam // Yś_68 //
children.translated_text: swiftly destroys the fierce poison of rabies, just as wind instantly disperses a mass of clouds. // Yś_68 //
Household soot combined with <s>mahiṣākṣa</s> (buffalo-eye berry), along with <s>vājigandhā</s> (Ashwagandha), ghee, and <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus)—

children.text: gomūtrapiṣṭo hy agado nihanti viṣāṇi saṃsthāvarajaṅgamāni // Yś_69 //
children.translated_text: this antidote, ground with cow's urine, destroys both plant-based and animal-based poisons. // Yś_69 //

<s>Māṃsī</s> (spikenard), <s>sevyā</s> (vetiver), <s>elā</s> (cardamom), <s>kauntī</s>, <s>jalada</s> (Cyperus), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), <s>rocanā</s> (ox bile pigment), <s>padmakeśara</s> (lotus stamens),
<s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>caṇḍā</s>, <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), antidote herbs, white <s>palitā</s>, <s>asṛglatā</s> (blood-vine), <s>padmaka</s> (wild cherry), and <s>elā</s> (cardamom)—
all in equal parts with eight parts of <s>gaura</s> (orpiment) and four parts of <s>ibhakusuma</s> (Woodfordia flower), these pills are suitable for use with all foods;
these antidote pills called <s>Candrodaya</s> (Moon-rise) destroy sorcery, misfortune, <s>piśāca</s> (demon) possession, fever, and poison. // Yś_70 //
<s>Siddhārtha</s> (white mustard), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>śirīṣa</s> (Albizia), <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora),
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Rubia), <s>rajanīdvaya</s> (the two turmerics), <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents), <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), and <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida)—
ground with goat's urine, this antidote is recommended for the removal of all spirit possessions,
destroying sorcery, madness, <s>piśāca</s> and <s>rākṣasa</s> spirits, when administered through drinking and other methods. // Yś_71 //
With cotton seeds, peacock feathers, <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), offering residues, and <s>piṇḍītaka</s>,
<s>tvak</s> (cinnamon), <s>vāṃśī</s> (bamboo), <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda), wasp stings, dung, husks, <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), hair, and snake slough,
<s>gośṛṅgī</s>, human teeth, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and <s>marica</s> (black pepper), all in equal parts, a fumigation is prepared
that is known to destroy <s>Skanda</s>-possession, madness, <s>piśāca</s> and <s>rākṣasa</s> spirits, divine possession, and fever. // Yś_72 //

With <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents), <s>dala</s> (bay leaf), <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>granthika</s>, alkali, <s>siṃhī</s>, <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), <s>siddhārtha</s> (white mustard), paired herbs, <s>ambu</s> (Cyperus), and <s>śakrāhvaya</s> (Wrightia),

sugar, <s>laśuna</s> (garlic), fruit, <s>trika</s> (three-part spice), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), <s>tiktā</s> (Picrorhiza), <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), <s>yaṣṭī</s> (licorice), <s>balā</s> (Sida), <s>lohitākhyā</s> (red-named herb), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), and <s>padmaka</s> (wild cherry),

yogurt, <s>tagara</s> (valerian), <s>madhūka</s> (Madhuca), heartwood, <s>priyāhvā</s> (Callicarpa), <s>viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s> (talc), with <s>cavya</s> (Piper chaba) and <s>amara</s>, all made into paste—

children.text: ghṛtam anavam aśeṣamūtrāmbusiddhaṃ smṛtaṃ bhūtarāvaṃ tu pānena tat syād grahaghnaṃ param // Yś_73 //
children.translated_text: fresh ghee prepared with all types of urine and water is known as <s>Bhūtarāva</s> (Terror of Spirits); taken by drinking, it is the supreme destroyer of spirit possessions. // Yś_73 //
antidote herbs, <s>śukataru</s> (parrot tree), flower, seeds, aquatic plants, <s>yaṣṭī</s> (licorice), <s>adrikarṇī</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>agni</s> (Plumbago), and <s>bilva</s> (Aegle)—
ghee prepared in equal parts as paste with the group of urines,

children.text: vidhivinihitam āśu sarvaiḥ kramair yojitaṃ hanti sarvagrahonmādakuṣṭhajvarāṃs tan mahābhūtarāvaṃ smṛtam // Yś_74 //
children.translated_text: properly prepared and applied through all methods, swiftly destroys all spirit possessions, madness, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), and fevers—that is known as <s>Mahābhūtarāva</s> (Great Terror of Spirits). // Yś_74 //

body.translated_text: With <s>nata</s> (Valeriana), <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), <s>lākṣā</s> (lac), <s>paṭolī</s> (pointed gourd), <s>samaṅgā</s> (Rubia), <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>siddhārtha</s> (white mustard), <s>siṃhī</s>, <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), paired herbs, <s>latā</s> (creeper), <s>rohiṇī</s> (Picrorhiza), fruit, <s>khadira</s> (Acacia), <s>kaṭutrikā</s> (three pungents), <s>kāṇḍa</s>, <s>dāru</s> (Cedrus), <s>krimighna</s> (anthelmintic herb), <s>ajagandhā</s>, <s>amarā</s>, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>kośātakī</s> (Luffa), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>ambu</s> (Cyperus), and <s>indrāhvaya</s> (Wrightia),

children.text: dārvī haridrā kuṭajasya bījaṃ siṃhī ca yaṣṭīmadhukaṃ ca tulyam /
children.translated_text: <s>Dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), seeds of <s>kuṭaja</s> (Holarrhena), <s>siṃhī</s>, and <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s> (licorice), in equal parts—

children.text: kvāthaḥ śiśoḥ stanyakṛte ca doṣe sarvātisāreṣu ca sarvajeṣu // Yś_75 //
children.translated_text: this decoction is for children in disorders caused by breast milk, and in all types of <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhea). // Yś_75 //

children.text: bilvaṃ ca puṣpāṇi ca dhātakīnāṃ jalaṃ salodhraṃ gajapippalī ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Bilva</s> (Aegle), flowers of <s>dhātakī</s> (Woodfordia), water with <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos), and <s>gajapippalī</s> (Scindapsus)—

children.text: kvāthāvalehau madhunā vimiśrau bāleṣu yojyāv atisāriteṣu // Yś_76 //
children.translated_text: the decoction and electuary, mixed with honey, should be administered to children suffering from <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhea). // Yś_76 //

children.text: śṛṅgīṃ sakṛṣṇātiviṣāṃ vicūrṇya lehaṃ vidadhyān madhunā śiśūnām /
children.translated_text: Having powdered <s>śṛṅgī</s> (Rhus) with <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper) and <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum), one should prepare a lick-medicine with honey for children.

children.text: kāsajvaracchardibhir arditānāṃ samākṣikāṃ cātiviṣām athaikām // Yś_77 //
children.translated_text: for those afflicted by cough, fever, and vomiting — or <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum) alone with honey. // Yś_77 //
A bronze vessel of <s>dhātrī</s> (Emblica) powder, saturated with its own juice, with equal parts of honey and ghee,
combined with eight <s>prasṛti</s> measures of black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), <s>mānī</s>, and sugar (<s>sitā</s>) — this, stored in a heap of ashes,

children.text: varṣānte tat samaśnan bhavati vipalito rūpavarṇaprabhāvī
children.translated_text: at the end of the rainy season, one who eats it regularly becomes grey-haired [no more], endowed with beauty, complexion, and influence,
free from disease, and possessed of intelligence, mental acuity, memory, eloquence, strength, stability, and vitality. // Yś_78 //
Licorice (<s>yaṣṭī</s>), <s>tugā</s>, rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>), with sugar (<s>śarkarā</s>) — <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits) combined [with these]

children.text: āyuḥpradā vṛṣyatamātimedhyā bhavej jarāvyādhivināśanī ca // Yś_79 //
children.translated_text: becomes life-giving, supremely aphrodisiac, highly intellect-promoting, and a destroyer of old age and disease. // Yś_79 //

children.text: cūrṇaṃ śvadaṃṣṭrāmalakāmṛtānāṃ lihet sasarpir madhunā ca yuktam /
children.translated_text: The powder of <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (Tribulus), <s>āmalaka</s> (Emblica), and <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora) — one should lick it with ghee and combined with honey;

children.text: vṛṣyaḥ sthiraḥ śāntavikāraduḥkhaḥ samāśataṃ jīvati kṛṣṇakeśaḥ // Yś_80 //
children.translated_text: one becomes virile, firm, with afflictions and suffering pacified, lives a hundred years, and has black hair. // Yś_80 //

children.text: nimbasya tailaṃ prakṛtistham evaṃ nasyāṃ niṣiktaṃ vidhinā yathāvat /
children.translated_text: The oil of neem (<s>nimba</s>) in its natural state, properly administered as nasal medication (<s>nasya</s>) according to procedure —

children.text: māsena tat kṣīraghṛtopayojyaṃ jarāprabhūtaṃ palitaṃ nihanti // Yś_81 //
children.translated_text: after one month, used together with milk and ghee, it destroys grey hair produced by old age. // Yś_81 //

children.text: gokṣurakaḥ kṣurakaḥ śatamūlī vānari nāgabalātibalā ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Gokṣuraka</s> (Tribulus), <s>kṣuraka</s>, <s>śatamūlī</s> (Asparagus), <s>vānarī</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, and <s>atibalā</s> —

children.text: cūrṇam idaṃ payasā niśi peyaṃ yasya gṛhe pramadāśatam asti // Yś_82 //
children.translated_text: this powder, drunk with milk at night, [is for] one in whose house there are a hundred women. // Yś_82 //

children.text: madhukāṃ madhunā ghṛtena ca pralihan kṣīram anuprayojayet /
children.translated_text: Licking licorice (<s>madhukā</s>) with honey and ghee, one should drink milk afterwards;

children.text: labhate ca na dhātusaṃkṣayaṃ pramadānāṃ ca śataṃ ca gacchati // Yś_83 //
children.translated_text: one does not suffer depletion of the bodily tissues (<s>dhātu</s>) and is capable of going to a hundred women. // Yś_83 //
A decoction of licorice (<s>yaṣṭī</s>) with the best salt, mixed with a paste of <s>kaliṅga</s>, black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), and fruit,

children.text: sakṣaudram etad vamanaṃ prayojyaṃ ghrāṇāsyakaṇṭhaśravaṇāmayeṣu // Yś_84 //
children.translated_text: combined with honey — this should be used as an emetic (<s>vamana</s>) in diseases of the nose, mouth, throat, and ears. // Yś_84 //
<s>Suvīra</s> (vinegar) boiled with <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula), combined with powder of <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum) root, black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), and <s>viḍa</s> salt,

children.text: virecanaṃ sorubutailam etan niratyayaṃ yojyam athāmayaghnam // Yś_85 //
children.translated_text: with castor oil — this purgative (<s>virecana</s>) is free from danger and should be applied; it destroys diseases. // Yś_85 //
<s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>rāṭha</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>amṛtalatā</s> (Tinospora), the five roots (<s>pañcamūlī</s>), and <s>balā</s> (Sida) —
combined with a meat broth, with portions of oil, salt, honey, ghee, and jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>),
with a paste of <s>puṣpāhvā</s>, <s>ghana</s> (Cyperus), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), <s>bilva</s> (Aegle), <s>phalinī</s>, black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), and <s>vacā</s> (Acorus),
this enema (<s>vasti</s>), combined with fermented gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), milk, and urine, is beneficial for wind-disorders (<s>vātāmaya</s>). // Yś_86 //
Oil prepared by cooking with <s>balā</s> (Sida) decoction and paste, containing fragrant <s>sugandhi</s> substances, with milk, curd, rice-washing water, whey, and vinegar (<s>cukra</s>),
likewise prepared individually with <s>sahacara</s>, <s>saraṇya</s>, and <s>amṛtāvarī</s> — each separately cooked, it is an unctuous enema (<s>anuvāsana</s>) that destroys wind. // Yś_87 //

children.text: nasyaṃ vidadhyād guḍanāgaraṃ vā sasaindhavāṃ māgadhikām athovā /
children.translated_text: One should administer as nasal medication (<s>nasya</s>) jaggery with dry ginger (<s>guḍanāgara</s>), or long pepper (<s>māgadhikā</s>) with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), or alternatively,
for diseases of the nose, mouth, neck, jaw, arm, back, head, eye, throat, and ears. // Yś_88 //

children.text: śreṣṭhaḥ parpaṭako jvareṣu vihitas tṛṣṇāsu pañcāmliko
children.translated_text: Best in fevers is <s>parpaṭaka</s>; for thirst, the five-sour preparation (<s>pañcāmlika</s>);

children.text: lājā cchardiṣu vastijeṣu girijo meheṣu dhātrīrasaḥ /
children.translated_text: parched rice (<s>lājā</s>) for vomiting; mineral pitch (<s>girija</s>) for urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>); <s>dhātrī</s> (Emblica) juice for bladder conditions;

children.text: rāsnā vātagadeṣu mūtram udare plīhāmaye pippalī
children.translated_text: <s>rāsnā</s> for wind diseases; urine for abdominal disease; long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>) for splenic disease;

children.text: saṃdhāne kṛmihā viṣe śukataruḥ śophe tathā gugguluḥ // Yś_89 //
children.translated_text: for healing [fractures], worm-destroying [agents]; <s>śukataru</s> for poison; and <s>guggulu</s> (resin) for swelling. // Yś_89 //

children.text: vṛṣo 'śrapitte kuṭajo 'tisāre bhallātam arśassu gareṣu hema /
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda) for blood-bile disorders; <s>kuṭaja</s> (Holarrhena) for diarrhea; <s>bhallātaka</s> (Semecarpus) for hemorrhoids; gold for poisoning;

children.text: sthūleṣu dāruḥ kṛmiṣu krimighnaṃ harītakī pāṇḍugadeṣu śasyate // Yś_90 //
children.translated_text: <s>dāru</s> (Cedrus) for obesity; <s>krimighna</s> (worm-destroying agents) for parasites; <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula) is recommended for jaundice (<s>pāṇḍu</s>). // Yś_90 //

children.text: akṣyāmayeṣu triphalā vadanti śūleṣu sarveṣu tathā rasonam /
children.translated_text: <s>Triphalā</s> (three fruits) is said [to be best] for eye diseases; garlic (<s>rasona</s>) for all types of colic (<s>śūla</s>);

children.text: kuṣṭheṣu nityaṃ khadirasya sāraṃ sarveṣu kāseṣu nidigdhikāṃ ca // Yś_91 //
children.translated_text: the heartwood of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia) always for skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>); and <s>nidigdhikā</s> (Solanum) for all types of cough. // Yś_91 //

children.text: śaṃsanti vājīkaraṇe śvadaṃṣṭrām uraḥkṣate nāgabalā balāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: They praise <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (Tribulus) as an aphrodisiac; <s>nāgabalā</s> and <s>balā</s> (Sida) for chest wounds (<s>uraḥkṣata</s>);

children.text: rasāyaneṣv āmalakaṃ sadevagraheṣu rogeṣu śilāhvayaṃ ca // Yś_92 //
children.translated_text: <s>āmalaka</s> (Emblica) for rejuvenation therapies (<s>rasāyana</s>); and the mineral called <s>śilā</s> (bitumen/shilajit) for diseases including spirit-seizures. // Yś_92 //

children.text: ity ete vidhivihitāḥ prasiddhayogāḥ siddhyarthaṃ vinigaditā bhiṣagvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: Thus these well-known formulations, composed according to proper procedure, have been expounded for the efficacy of the best physicians;

children.text: dṛṣṭvaitān katham acikitsako 'pi yuñjyād ity arthaṃ punar api vakṣyate 'tra kiṃcit // Yś_93 //
children.translated_text: having seen these, [one may ask] how even a non-physician might apply them — for this purpose, something more will be stated here. // Yś_93 //
By suppression [of natural urges], fasting, staying awake, speaking loudly, exercise, travel, and by pungent, bitter, astringent, and dry [substances],

children.text: cintāvyavāyabhayalaṅghanaśokaśītair vāyuḥ prakopam upayāti ghanāgame ca // Yś_94 //
children.translated_text: by worry, sexual intercourse, fear, fasting, grief, and cold — <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) becomes aggravated; and also at the onset of the rains. // Yś_94 //
By pungent, sour, alcoholic, salty, hot, burning, sharp [substances], by anger, fire, sunlight, exertion, and dry vegetables,

children.text: kṣārādyajīrṇaviṣamāśanabhojanaś ca pittaṃ prakopam upayāti ghanātyaye ca // Yś_95 //
children.translated_text: by alkaline [substances], indigestion, irregular eating, and food — <s>Pitta</s> (bile) becomes aggravated; and also at the end of the rains. // Yś_95 //
By sleeping during the day, by sweet, cool, fatty, fish, meat, heavy, sour, slimy, sesame, sugarcane, and milk products,

children.text: snigdhātitṛptilavaṇodakapānabhakṣaiḥ śleṣmā prakopam upayāti tathā vasante // Yś_96 //
children.translated_text: by unctuous [substances], excessive satiation, salty [substances], water, drinks, and foods — <s>Śleṣman</s> (phlegm) becomes aggravated; and likewise in spring. // Yś_96 //

children.text: ity evam ete kramaśo dviśo vā doṣāḥ pravṛddhā yugapat trayo vā /
children.translated_text: Thus these <s>doṣas</s> (humors), increased successively, in pairs,

children.text: kurvanti rogān vividhān śarīre saṃkhyātu saṃjnāvigatān anekān // Yś_97 //
children.translated_text: or all three simultaneously, produce various diseases in the body — innumerable, known by different names. // Yś_97 //
Roughness, contraction, piercing pain, colic, darkening of complexion, limb-ache, cracking, restless movements,

children.text: suptatvaśītatvakharatvaśoṣān karmāṇi vāyoḥ pravadanti tajjñāḥ // Yś_98 //
children.translated_text: numbness, coldness, harshness, and desiccation — those who know declare these to be the actions of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind). // Yś_98 //
Discharge, sweating, burning, redness, foul odor, maceration, suppuration, irritability,

children.text: pralāpamūrchabhramapītabhāvān pittasya karmāṇi vadanti tajjñāḥ // Yś_99 //
children.translated_text: delirium, fainting, dizziness, and yellowish discoloration — those who know declare these to be the actions of <s>Pitta</s> (bile). // Yś_99 //
Whiteness, coldness, heaviness, itching, unctuousness, coating, stiffness, adhesion,

children.text: utsekasaṃghātacirakriyāś ca kaphasya karmāṇi vadanti tajjnāḥ // Yś_100 //
children.translated_text: nausea, congestion, and slow-acting [nature] — those who know declare these to be the actions of <s>Kapha</s> (phlegm). // Yś_100 //

children.text: etāni liṅgāni ca tatkṛtānāṃ sarvāmayānām api naikanāmnām /
children.translated_text: These are the signs of diseases caused by them, which have many different names;

children.text: kaścid bhavet prāptiviśeṣa eṣāṃ saṃjñāntaraṃ yena tu saṃprayānti // Yś_101 //
children.translated_text: there may be some special occurrence of these [signs], whereby they acquire a different designation. // Yś_101 //
By sluggishness, drowsiness, impurity of the heart, non-movement of the <s>doṣas</s>, absence of hunger, and [scanty] urine,
by heaviness of the abdomen, loss of appetite, and numbness — they declare the disease to be accompanied by <s>āma</s> (undigested matter). // Yś_102 //
By unctuous, hot, stable, aphrodisiac, strengthening, salty, sweet, sour, oily substances, sunbathing,
bathing, anointing, enema, meat, wine, massage, and rubbing,
oleation, sudation, decoction enema, nasal therapy, palliative treatment, unctuous poultice, and similar [measures] —
this regimen of drink, food, conduct, and medicine leads to the pacification of <s>Vāta</s> (wind). // Yś_103 //
Bitter, sweet, astringent, cool substances, wind, shade, night, fanning,
moonlight, earth, a house, mechanical devices, water, clouds, and the touch of a woman's body,
ghee, milk, purgation, irrigation, bloodletting, ointment, and similar [measures] —

children.text: pānāhāravihārabheṣajam idaṃ pittaṃ praśāntiṃ nayet // Yś_104 //
children.translated_text: this regimen of drink, food, conduct, and medicine leads to the pacification of <s>Pitta</s> (bile). // Yś_104 //
Dry, alkaline, astringent, bitter, pungent substances, exercise, expectoration,
sexual activity, walking, fighting, staying awake, water-sport, and foot-striking,
smoke, very hot [substances], head-purgation, emesis, sudation, fasting, and similar [measures] —

children.text: pānāhāravihārabhaiṣajam idaṃ śleṣmānam ugraṃ jayet // Yś_105 //
children.translated_text: this regimen of drink, food, conduct, and medicine conquers severe <s>Śleṣman</s> (phlegm). // Yś_105 //
One should conquer <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) by fasting, <s>kola</s> (jujube) gruel, light food, thin soup, water, and bitter broths,

children.text: virūkṣaṇasvedanapācanaiś ca saṃśodhanair ūrdhvam adhas tathā ca // Yś_106 //
children.translated_text: and by drying, sudation, digestive [measures], and purification — both upward and downward. // Yś_106 //
In winter, the rains, and the cold season, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) [is aggravated]; in the watery season and the hot season, <s>Pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: kaphasya kopaḥ kusumāgame ca kurvanti tad vai vihitaṃ yathaiṣām // Yś_107 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kapha</s> (phlegm) is aggravated in spring — one should treat each according to what is prescribed for them. // Yś_107 //

children.text: kaphasya kope vamanaṃ sanasyaṃ virecanaṃ pittabhave vikāre /
children.translated_text: When <s>Kapha</s> is aggravated, emesis (<s>vamana</s>) with nasal therapy (<s>nasya</s>) [is indicated]; purgation (<s>virecana</s>) in disorders arising from <s>Pitta</s>;

children.text: vātātmake vastim udāharanti saṃsargaje 'pi vyatimiśram etat // Yś_108 //
children.translated_text: for conditions dominated by <s>Vāta</s>, they prescribe enema (<s>vasti</s>); and in conditions of combined [<s>doṣas</s>], a mixed [treatment]. // Yś_108 //
<s>Vāta</s> [is pacified] by sour, oily, salty substances and sweet food and drink; <s>Pitta</s> likewise by sweet, bitter, astringent, and cool [substances];

children.text: śleṣmāpi tiktakaṭurūkṣakaṣāyatīkṣṇair āmaṃ praśāntim upayānty apatarpaṇena // Yś_109 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣman</s> (phlegm) also by bitter, pungent, dry, astringent, and sharp [substances]; and <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) attains pacification by non-nourishing [therapy]. // Yś_109 //

children.text: buddhvaitad anyad api yat tad anuktam atra yuktyā svayaṃ samadhigamya yathānurūpam /
children.translated_text: Having understood this, whatever else has not been stated here — having ascertained it by one's own reasoning, according to what is appropriate,

children.text: rogeṣu bheṣajam analpamatir vidadhyāc chāstraṃ hi kiṃcid upadeśalavaṃ karoti // Yś_110 //
children.translated_text: a physician of no small intelligence should administer medicine for diseases; for the treatise provides only a drop of instruction. // Yś_110 //

children.text: guṇādhikaṃ yogaśataṃ nibadhya prāptaṃ mayā puṇyam anuttaraṃ yat /
children.translated_text: Having composed this <s>Yogaśataka</s> (Hundred Medical Formulations) of superior qualities, the unsurpassed merit that I have obtained —

children.text: nānāprakārāmayanīḍabhūtaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat tena bhavatv arogam // Yś_111 //
children.translated_text: by that, may the entire world, which is the abode of manifold diseases, become free from illness. // Yś_111 //
